questions.stem: This colorized transmission electron micrograph shows virions of a hemorrhagic fever virus family. Which structural feature is characteristic of the particles shown?

explanation.summary: The image shows long, thread-like enveloped virions typical of the Filoviridae family (Marburg/Ebola), which have a helical nucleocapsid enclosed in an envelope and a filamentous morphology.
explanation.whyCorrect: The image shows long, thread-like enveloped virions typical of the Filoviridae family (Marburg/Ebola), which have a helical nucleocapsid enclosed in an envelope and a filamentous morphology.

questions.stem: This animal appears in a section on filovirus transmission. What is its epidemiologic role for Marburg virus?

explanation.summary: Bats serve as the natural reservoir for Marburg virus and the likely reservoir for Ebola virus; spillover into humans occurs through contact with infected animal fluids.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bats serve as the natural reservoir for Marburg virus and the likely reservoir for Ebola virus; spillover into humans occurs through contact with infected animal fluids.

questions.stem: This animal is shown in the hantavirus epidemiology section. How do humans most commonly acquire hantavirus infection from it?

explanation.summary: Rodents are the reservoir for hantaviruses; humans are infected mainly by inhaling aerosolized particles from rodent feces, urine, and saliva.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rodents are the reservoir for hantaviruses; humans are infected mainly by inhaling aerosolized particles from rodent feces, urine, and saliva.

questions.stem: This schematic maps where FDA-approved monoclonal antibody therapies bind on the Ebola virus surface glycoprotein. By what mechanism do these antibodies neutralize the virus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocking glycoprotein binding to host cell receptors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blocking viral budding from the membrane

explanation.summary: The monoclonal antibodies bind the viral surface glycoprotein and block its engagement of cognate host receptors, neutralizing the virus; they also mediate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The monoclonal antibodies bind the viral surface glycoprotein and block its engagement of cognate host receptors, neutralizing the virus; they also mediate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.
